docs.title: NOMAD ML Workflows
docs.text: nomad-ml-workflows helps you turn NOMAD entries into reusable datasets and describe machine learning models alongside their artifacts, training metadata, and evaluations.

docs.title: Choose an export action
docs.text:
Action Use it for Output Export Entries Complete archives or selected archive paths from this deployment JSON, CSV, or a Parquet dataset in a staging project/upload Export Forces Atomic structures with selected energies, forces, and stresses; shown as Export MLIP Data Action in the GUI Extended XYZ or an ASE database in a staging project/upload Export Remote Entries Entries from configured Oases, optionally including this deployment One export per target in S3, optionally copied into a local staging project/upload

Each action runs independently. They share permission-scoped search and archive extraction, with Export Entries providing the foundation. Read the export explanation for selection, formats, manifests, and counts.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow the short Export Entries tutorial to save up to ten visible entries as JSON in a ZIP, using either the GUI or a Python REST client. Use the action chooser for task-specific guides.

Administrators can follow installation and configuration to enable the plugin, start a CPU worker, set limits, and configure remote targets and storage.

docs.title: Describe a model
docs.text: The ML model schema describes models independently of their implementation library and artifact format. Record model versions, libraries, files, training datasets, and evaluation metrics in a NOMAD entry. The related Dataset schema can describe data through NOMAD references, files, or URLs.

docs.title: Export functionality
docs.text: The three export actions share a sequence: search entries using the initiating user's permissions, record the selected entry IDs in a manifest, read their archives, write the requested format, and publish the artifacts. Export Entries supplies this foundation; Export Forces converts archives into atomic structures, while Export Remote Entries runs extraction on selected deployments and saves each dataset to S3. You can start any action independently.

docs.title: Search selection and archive content
docs.text:
search_settings.query is a NOMAD search query encoded as JSON text, for example "{\"entry_type\": \"ELNSample\"}" in a JSON input file. Copy the query object from View API Call in a search app and encode that object as text; do not copy the whole API request body. The query determines which entries match.

search_settings.owner determines the ownership scope:

Value Eligible entries visible All entries visible to the initiating user; the default public Public entries user The user's entries shared The user's entries and entries shared with them staging The user's and shared unpublished entries

max_entries is a positive selection limit. Its default is the smaller of 1,000 and the configured deployment cap. The action selects up to the applicable limit from the search results; it does not sample randomly.

For Export Entries and Export Remote Entries, search_settings.required controls what is read from each selected archive. An empty list requests the complete archive. Include directives use dot-separated section or quantity paths, such as results.method. Set resolve_references: true on a path to include data reached through references below it, subject to access permissions. Only include directives are currently supported by the public input model. Choosing a path does not filter out entries where that path is absent; use the search query to require matching content.

Export Forces instead uses search_settings.properties to select energies, forces, and stresses. It adds corresponding quantity-presence conditions to its search query and reads the archive data needed by the forces exporter.

docs.title: Formats and packaging
docs.text:
Format Representation json A JSON array of records containing entry_id, upload_id, and the selected archive; preserves archive structure parquet One row per exported entry, with archive sections flattened into columns and nested quantity values preserved; written as a directory of parts sharing one schema csv Flattened archive columns; nested values are encoded as JSON text in cells extxyz / ase_db Atomic structures and selected properties, available through Export Forces

Tabular export follows the installed NOMAD metainfo definitions. Data without a corresponding current schema definition may be omitted or an entry may be skipped; consult the action logs when counts differ. JSON is useful when preserving the archive structure is the priority.

export_settings.create_zip_archive defaults to true. Local actions put a ZIP into the destination upload's raw files. With false, they create a subdirectory containing the same artifacts. Remote export uses an S3 object for ZIP output or an S3 prefix for directory output.

docs.title: Manifest, metadata, and counts
docs.text:
Every successful export includes selected_entries.json, an ordered list of selected entry_id/upload_id pairs, and metadata.json. Metadata contains a note, a schema, and a data object with the original inputs, search timestamps, deployment host, package versions, and these fields:

Field under data Meaning num_entries_available Total search matches before applying the selection limit num_entries_selected Entries recorded in the manifest after applying the limit num_entries_exported Exported archive records or tabular rows for Export Entries; Export Forces records the selected manifest count, which is not a count of atomic configurations reached_max_entries_limit Whether the total matches exceeded the selection limit error_info Extraction error information, when recorded

The manifest records selection, not a guarantee that every archive could be read or converted. Check counts and logs before using a dataset. A search with zero matches still produces metadata and an empty manifest, but no data artifact. This applies to the forces export and each remote extraction as well.

Remote export returns per-target results. Counts are summed across targets without deduplication, so the same entry on multiple deployments may contribute more than once.

docs.title: Models and datasets
docs.text: Exports produce files that you can use in downstream training. The separate MLModel and Dataset schemas describe model artifacts and their provenance. Running an export does not automatically create an MLModel or Dataset entry, train a model, or compute evaluation metrics.

docs.title: ML model schema
docs.text: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.model.MLModel describes a machine learning model independently of its implementation library and artifact format. It is a NOMAD schema that can be used as an entry's data section and edited in the ELN. It records the model and its provenance; it does not load model weights, run training, or calculate evaluation scores.

docs.title: Model identity and implementation
docs.text:
Alongside the inherited Entity metadata, such as name, MLModel provides:

Field Meaning architecture Architecture or model family, such as resnet or U-Net model_version Your version identifier for this model license License under which the model is available tasks List of intended tasks tags Free-form discovery labels libraries Repeatable records, each with name and version

The task and library editors offer suggestions from the Hugging Face model-tag catalog. These suggestions are optional UI metadata: a temporary catalog/network failure leaves them empty without preventing the schema from loading. Recording a model does not require uploading it to Hugging Face.

docs.title: Artifacts and normalization
docs.text:
artifacts is repeatable, so one model can refer to multiple files, such as weights and a separate model representation. Each artifact has model_file (a path relative to the upload's raw files), format, file_size in bytes, and checksum.

During normalization, an existing artifact file supplies its size, replacing any previously recorded file_size. If format is missing, the final file extension supplies it in lowercase: weights.PT yields pt. An explicitly supplied format is preserved. A missing file causes a warning and does not supply size or format.

Checksums are supplied metadata: normalization does not calculate or verify them. Record the algorithm with the value, for example using a sha256: prefix. Evaluation results are also supplied metadata and are not recomputed.

docs.title: Training and evaluation
docs.text:
The single training subsection records epochs, batch_size, a dataset reference, and dataset_split (for example, train). Its optional optimizer subsection records name and learning_rate.

evaluations is repeatable. Each record holds one metric_name/metric_value pair, a dataset reference, and a dataset_split, such as test. Use separate records for different metrics, datasets, or splits, and make metric names precise enough to explain their scale and units.

The related nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.dataset.Dataset schema describes datasets using references to NOMAD sections/entries, files containing raw-file paths, and/or external resource urls. Training and evaluation references point to a Dataset section; dataset_split labels the portion used without creating or enforcing that split. An export action produces files, which you can describe in a Dataset entry yourself.

docs.title: Small archive example
docs.text:
Save the following as model.archive.yaml in a NOMAD upload with the model schema enabled:

data:
  m_def: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.model.MLModel
  name: Example image classifier
  architecture: resnet
  model_version: "1.0"
  license: MIT
  tasks: [image-classification]
  tags: [example]
  libraries:
    - name: pytorch
      version: "2.5"
  artifacts:
    - model_file: models/weights.pt
      format: pytorch-state-dict
  training:
    epochs: 20
    batch_size: 32
    dataset_split: train
    optimizer:
      name: Adam
      learning_rate: 0.001
  evaluations:
    - metric_name: Accuracy (fraction)
      metric_value: 0.91
      dataset_split: test

Upload your actual weights at models/weights.pt to let normalization record their size. The explicit format remains pytorch-state-dict. Supply an actual checksum if available; the example leaves it unset. The evaluation value illustrates manually recorded metadata.

To connect provenance, create a separate Dataset entry and use its reference in training.dataset and each applicable evaluations[].dataset field through the reference editor. For example, a Dataset's own data can be:

data:
  m_def: nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages.dataset.Dataset
  name: Classifier data
  files:
    - datasets/images.zip

Replace this raw-file path with your dataset's location in its upload. Use references for NOMAD archive sections or urls for externally hosted data when those better describe your dataset.

docs.title: Export entries
docs.text: Use Export Entries Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries) to save local NOMAD archives as JSON, CSV, or Parquet. The tutorial demonstrates the GUI and a Python REST submission.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need access to the action and source entries, a writable staging project/upload for the output, and a running CPU action worker. Administrators can follow installation and configuration.

docs.title: Select entries and content
docs.text:
1. Find your entries in a NOMAD search app and copy the query object from View API Call.
  2. Open Actions → Run action → Export Entries Action and set Destination project ID to your staging upload ID.
  3. Choose the ownership scope, a positive maximum entry count, and the search query. In the GUI, enter the query as JSON text; in an input JSON file, encode it as a string.
  4. Leave Archive required paths empty for full archives, or add include paths and enable reference resolution where needed.
  5. Select json, parquet, or csv, choose ZIP or directory output, and run the action.
Input Meaning upload_id Destination staging upload; separate from the uploads selected by the query search_settings.owner visible (default), public, user, shared, or staging search_settings.max_entries Positive limit, bounded by the deployment cap; default is at most 1,000 search_settings.query Search query as JSON text; selects entries search_settings.required Include directives with type, path, and resolve_references; selects archive content export_settings.file_format parquet (default), csv, or json export_settings.create_zip_archive true (default) for ZIP; false for an upload subdirectory

For example, this action input selects up to 100 public entries with entry_type equal to ELNSample, then exports their results.method sections as Parquet:

{
  "upload_id": "YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID",
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "public",
    "max_entries": 100,
    "query": "{\"entry_type\": \"ELNSample\"}",
    "required": [
      {
        "type": "include",
        "path": "results.method",
        "resolve_references": false
      }
    ]
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "parquet",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

Replace the query and paths with ones appropriate to your entries. An include path does not require the entry to contain that path; search filters and archive-content selection have different roles. To follow references beneath an included path, set its resolve_references to true. Exclusion directives are not supported by the public input model.

For REST, wrap this input in {"data": input_json} as shown in the tutorial. Omit user_id; NOMAD supplies the authenticated user's ID.

docs.title: Retrieve and inspect the export
docs.text:
Monitor the action instance's status and logs. After success, its exported_dir_path gives the ZIP filename or directory path relative to the destination upload's raw files; workflow_duration reports elapsed seconds. Open the project's files to download it.

Artifact Contents data.json JSON array of records containing entry_id, upload_id, and the selected archive data.csv Flattened columns, with nested values as JSON text data.parquet/part-NNNNN.parquet Parquet parts sharing a schema; nested quantity values are preserved selected_entries.json Selected entry_id/upload_id pairs metadata.json Inputs, counts, timing, deployment/package versions, and a JSON schema

Only the selected data format is produced. Read the whole extracted Parquet directory with PyArrow:

import pyarrow.parquet as pq

table = pq.read_table('data.parquet')

Compare num_entries_available, num_entries_selected, and num_entries_exported under metadata's data object. The manifest describes selection; archive-read or flattening failures may reduce the exported count. Inspect logs for skipped entries. A zero-match export contains metadata and an empty manifest, with no data artifact. See manifest and count semantics.

docs.title: Export energies, forces, and stresses
docs.text:
Use Export MLIP Data Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces) to export atomic structures and selected properties for machine learning interatomic potentials. Its formats are Extended XYZ (extxyz) and ASE database (ase_db).

Currently only DFT entries are supported.

magmoms are currently only added for VASP DFT entries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need access to the action and compatible calculation archives, a writable staging project/upload, and a running CPU action worker with the cpu-action dependencies installed, including nomad-forces-export. See administrator setup.

docs.title: Configure and run
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Run action → Export MLIP Data Action and set the destination staging upload ID.
  2. Choose an ownership scope and maximum entry count. Keep or adapt the prefilled calculation query for your source data.
{ 
  "results.method.method_name:any": [ "DFT" ],   
  "quantities:all": 
    [ "run.calculation", 
      "run.system" ] 
}
  1. Under Properties, select energies, forces, and/or stresses. The underlying field names are exactly energies, forces, and stresses; each defaults to false.
  2. Choose extxyz and/or ase_db, select ZIP or directory output, and run the action.
  3. Inspect status, logs, and results, then download the output from the destination project's files using exported_dir_path.

The action adds quantity-presence conditions for the selected properties to the query (run.calculation.energy.total_t0.value, run.calculation.forces.total.value, and run.calculation.stress.total.value). Use archives supported by nomad-forces-export; general ELN entries need not contain compatible structures or calculation data.

docs.title: Example input
docs.text:
This input requests energy and force data from up to 100 public matching entries. {} adds no user filters; the action still adds the selected property requirements. For a narrower dataset, use a query copied from a search app's View API Call dialog.

{
  "upload_id": "YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID",
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "public",
    "max_entries": 100,
    "query": "{}",
    "properties": {
      "energies": true,
      "forces": true,
      "stresses": false
    }
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "extxyz",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

For REST, omit user_id and send the input under data to this action's start endpoint. query is JSON text. Ownership scopes and limits follow the shared selection rules. Forces uses properties instead of an archive required list; its extractor chooses the archive content needed for atomic data.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
The ZIP or directory contains data.xyz for Extended XYZ or data.db for an ASE database, plus selected_entries.json and metadata.json. Set file_format to ase_db for database output, or create_zip_archive to false for a directory. The result also reports workflow_duration.

Metadata records source selection, inputs, versions, and timing.

num_entries_exported is set to the number of entries that were processed; it does not measure the number of exported atomic configurations. An entry can contain multiple configurations, and conversion may skip unsupported frames. The archive filtering checks for relevant properties being present before adding a entry to the count, however due to errors within the archive data there might be no usable frames in that entry.

num_frames_exported gives the actual total number of frames exported acroos all the entries.

Inspect logs and the generated atomic dataset to assess its contents.

A zero-match run produces an empty manifest and metadata without data.xyz or data.db. See the shared export explanation for packaging and provenance.

docs.title: Export remote entries
docs.text: Use Export Remote Entries Action (nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries) to run the same archive extraction on configured Oases over Temporal Nexus. Each target writes its own export to S3. You can also include the local deployment and copy successful exports into a local staging upload.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
An administrator must configure Nexus endpoints, action access, storage, and CPU workers on participating deployments; see remote export setup. The initiating user's ID is forwarded to remote extraction, which applies that user's permissions there. Participating deployments must recognize that identity and trust the Nexus connection.

S3 storage must be accessible to the workers that write exports and, when copying to a local upload, to the initiating deployment's worker. A local writable staging upload is needed only when save_to_upload is true. The default action access is restricted to users: [admin]; administrators must configure the intended user IDs or groups.

docs.title: Choose targets and run
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Run action → Export Remote Entries Action.
  2. Choose one or more Target Oases. local runs extraction on this deployment; other values are administrator-configured Nexus target keys.
  3. Set search options, including ownership scope, maximum entries, query JSON text, and optional archive include paths. The selection limit applies separately to each target.
  4. Select json, csv, or parquet and ZIP or directory output.
  5. Leave Save dataset to upload disabled for S3-only output, or enable it and provide the destination staging upload ID.
  6. Run the action, then inspect every target's result.

docs.title: Example input
docs.text:
With the administrator's oasis-b target configured and deployment-managed storage (s3_mode: env), this input exports up to ten visible entries from both local and remote deployments:

{
  "target_oases": ["local", "oasis-b"],
  "save_to_upload": false,
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "visible",
    "max_entries": 10,
    "query": "{}",
    "required": []
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "json",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

Use the keys supplied by your administrator. To search only remote data, omit local from target_oases. To copy each successful dataset to a local upload, set save_to_upload to true and add upload_id. Each target remains a separate export; the action does not merge datasets.

For REST, omit user_id and submit this input under data. Search query text and archive include directives follow Export Entries. Remote export does not produce forces formats.

docs.title: Storage options
docs.text:
In the default env mode, the worker resolves storage from deployment configuration and environment variables, and the form hides storage_settings. Supplied storage settings are replaced by deployment-managed values on a deployment running in this mode.

If the administrator enables s3_mode: workflow_input, add this storage_settings object to the action input:

{
  "storage_settings": {
    "storage_type": "s3",
    "bucket": "ml-datasets",
    "prefix": "exports",
    "region": "eu-central-1"
  }
}

This fragment supplements the complete input above. endpoint_url can select an S3-compatible service; optional access_key_id, secret_access_key, and session_token supply explicit credentials. Without explicit credentials, the S3 client can use its configured credential chain. Explicit credentials are serialized into workflow payloads, so use deployment-managed credentials where possible. A remote deployment in env mode resolves its own storage even when the caller supplies settings; the caller must be able to read that storage if local copying is requested.

docs.title: Inspect the results
docs.text:
Result field Meaning results Mapping from each target key to its execution summary results.<target>.status SUCCESS or FAILED results.<target>.is_remote Whether the target used Nexus results.<target>.num_entries_exported Exported count for that target results.<target>.remote_uri Download URL or S3 URI on success; use only after checking status results.<target>.error_message Target failure details, when present total_entries_exported Sum across targets, without deduplication remote_uri Primary URI, preferring local output; inspect per-target results for usable locations workflow_duration Total elapsed seconds

A remote target can report FAILED while other targets succeed and the parent workflow completes. A failure in local execution can fail the parent workflow. Local copying is part of each target's execution and can fail after its S3 output was written; inspect logs as well as results.

Successful S3 ZIPs or prefixes contain the same data artifact, manifest, and metadata as Export Entries. ZIP output normally returns a presigned download URL with a requested lifetime of two days (subject to credential expiry), falling back to an s3:// URI if signing fails. Directory output returns an s3:// prefix. Zero-match targets still write metadata and an empty manifest, without a data artifact. If copying was requested, find the copied ZIPs or directories in the destination project's files. The action returns storage locations rather than local upload paths.

docs.title: Install and configure the plugin
docs.text: This guide is for administrators of an existing NOMAD deployment. Install the plugin in the environments or images used by the API and action workers, and apply matching plugin configuration. For container deployments, build these dependencies into the deployment images. See the NOMAD Oasis configuration guide for deployment-wide plugin configuration.

docs.title: Install dependencies and enable entry points
docs.text:
The package requires nomad-lab>=1.4.3. Install the worker dependencies with the cpu-action extra:

pip install 'nomad-ml-workflows[cpu-action]'

The extra supplies PyArrow for tabular output, boto3 for S3, and nomad-forces-export for atomic data. The base installation provides the schema packages and action registration; CPU workers need the extra to execute all export formats.

The plugin registers these entry points:

Entry point Purpose nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries Local archive export nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces Atomic structures and properties nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries Nexus and S3 export nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages:dataset_schema Dataset schema nomad_ml_workflows.schema_packages:model_schema ML model schema

Ensure the required entry points are included in your deployment's plugin selection and are not excluded. Configure action options under plugins.entry_points.options as below. Restart the API and CPU workers after installation or configuration changes. Confirm the actions are offered by the GUI or authenticated GET /actions/schemas relative to the deployment's API base URL.

docs.title: Configure Temporal and start the CPU worker
docs.text:
The API and workers must connect to the same Temporal service and namespace. For a service reachable as temporal:7233, add this to nomad.yaml:

temporal:
  enabled: true
  host: temporal
  port: 7233
  namespace: default

Replace the host and namespace with your deployment's values, and configure its required Temporal authentication. Start a CPU action worker in the configured NOMAD environment:

nomad admin run action-cpu-worker

In the nomad-distro-dev workspace, the existing uv run poe cpuworker task starts this worker with the local configuration. The root uv run poe start task starts the development API/app worker; run the CPU worker alongside it.

The CPU worker polls cpu-task-queue, where all three export actions run. Submission can succeed without a polling worker, leaving the action waiting to execute. Workers need access to NOMAD's database, search index, archive/raw storage, and shared action-artifact storage. Ensure filesystem paths and permissions are consistent across the workers that may run an action's activities.

docs.title: Set limits and action access
docs.text:
Merge this example into the existing nomad.yaml, replacing the example user and group IDs:

plugins:
  entry_points:
    options:
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries:
        max_entries_export_limit: 100000
        read_archives_timeout: 7200
        write_tabular_timeout: 7200
        max_write_buffer_size_bytes: 67108864
        max_write_buffer_size_rows: 1024
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_forces:
        max_entries_export_limit: 100000
        export_archives_timeout: 10800
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]

Limits must be positive; 0 does not mean unlimited. The shared manifest activity uses the Export Entries cap, including for forces and remote exports. Forces also validates its input against its own cap; keep the two caps aligned when you want the same limit. A remote search applies the executing deployment's cap separately for each target.

Timeouts are in seconds. The two tabular buffer limits control buffered rows and encoded input bytes, not a hard process-memory ceiling; one oversized row can exceed the byte target. Optionally set MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 in the CPU worker environment before startup when using PyArrow with mimalloc to release unused pages more promptly.

users and groups contain NOMAD IDs. A user is allowed if their ID is listed or they belong to a listed group. Empty or unset restrictions allow authenticated users to start the action. Entry permissions still apply to searches. Remote export defaults to users: [admin]; replace it with intended IDs, or set users: [] and a nonempty groups list for group-only access.

docs.title: Configure remote export
docs.text: Enable the remote action and its Nexus handler on the receiving deployment as well as the initiating one. Each deployment needs an active CPU worker. Their identity setup must recognize the forwarded user ID, and their Temporal infrastructure must permit the Nexus connection.

docs.title: Register the Nexus endpoint
docs.text:
For deployments using different namespaces on one Temporal service, register oasis-b on that service, routing to the receiving namespace's CPU queue:

temporal operator nexus endpoint create \
  --name oasis-b \
  --target-namespace oasis-b-namespace \
  --target-task-queue cpu-task-queue

temporal operator nexus endpoint get --name oasis-b

Use your CLI connection and authentication settings for that service. Endpoint creation runs once per endpoint name. Separate Temporal services require an externally routed Nexus endpoint and corresponding network/authentication setup; a namespace on another service cannot be reached by the worker-target example alone. See the Temporal CLI operator reference for endpoint and connection options.

docs.title: Configure targets and S3
docs.text:
Merge this configuration on the initiating deployment:

plugins:
  entry_points:
    options:
      nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_remote_entries:
        users: [EXPORT_USER_ID]
        groups: [EXPORT_GROUP_ID]
        local_display_name: Local Oasis
        nexus_endpoints:
          oasis-b:
            display_name: Oasis B
            endpoint: oasis-b
        s3_mode: env
        s3_bucket: ml-datasets
        s3_prefix: exports
        s3_region: eu-central-1

Use the same name for the mapping key (oasis-b), the endpoint value, and the registered Nexus endpoint. Current dispatch uses the selected mapping key as the endpoint name. local is reserved for local execution. The display name is only a GUI label.

The default s3_mode: env resolves storage on each executing deployment. Set an accessible bucket and credentials on each deployment; configuring the initiating worker alone does not configure a receiver. For optional copying back to a local upload, the initiating worker must also be able to read the receiver's storage, using a compatible endpoint and credentials. Using the same S3 service and accessible bucket across participating deployments is a straightforward setup.

Entry point option Environment fallback s3_bucket S3_BUCKET, AWS_S3_BUCKET, AWS_BUCKET s3_prefix S3_PREFIX, AWS_S3_PREFIX s3_endpoint_url S3_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL s3_region S3_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_REGION s3_access_key_id S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID s3_secret_access_key S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY s3_session_token S3_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN

Entry point values take precedence over the fallbacks, which are checked in the listed order. If explicit credentials are absent, boto3 can use the worker's configured credential chain. Set s3_endpoint_url for an S3-compatible service. Workers need permission to write export objects; copying ZIPs requires object reads, and copying directories also requires listing the export prefix. Credential fields are serialized for workflow execution, including when resolved from the environment, so restrict access to Temporal payloads and history.

Alternatively, set s3_mode: workflow_input to show and require storage_settings in the action form. Configure participating receivers the same way if they should use the caller's supplied settings. A receiver in env mode replaces them with its own deployment settings. See the remote guide for an input example.

docs.title: Verify the deployment
docs.text: Run the small Export Entries tutorial, check the action instance completes, and inspect the ZIP in its destination upload. For remote setup, start with a single configured target and a small limit, check its per-target status and storage location, then enable local copying if needed. Search and export counts are explained in the export overview.

docs.title: Choose an export action
docs.text:
Sign in to a deployment with the plugin enabled and an active CPU action worker. For output saved to NOMAD, create or choose a writable staging project/upload and copy its ID. Source entries may belong to other uploads, provided you can read them.

Your task Guide GUI action name Export local archives or selected paths as JSON, CSV, or Parquet Export entries Export Entries Action Export atomic structures with energies, forces, or stresses Export forces Export MLIP Data Action Search configured Oases and save results in S3 Export remote entries Export Remote Entries Action

For a first export, follow the GUI and REST tutorial. All JSON action-input examples in these guides omit user_id: NOMAD injects the authenticated user's ID when starting an action through REST, including from the GUI.

Open Actions, select Run action, choose an action, complete its form, and submit it. Use the action instance page to monitor status, inspect results, and read logs. Actions available to you depend on the deployment's configured user/group access.

If an action is missing or remains waiting to execute, consult the administrator's installation guide. For format and count semantics, read the export explanation.

docs.title: Export ten entries through the GUI or REST
docs.text: This tutorial exports up to ten entries visible to you as JSON, packaged in a ZIP saved to a staging project/upload. Both interfaces below run Export Entries with the same inputs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Sign in to a NOMAD deployment with Export Entries Action enabled.
  • Create or choose a writable, unpublished project/upload and copy its ID.
  • Ask the administrator to confirm that the CPU worker is running. It must poll Temporal's task queue to execute the workflow; REST submission can succeed while execution waits for a worker.

docs.title: Use the GUI
docs.text:
1. Open Actions and select Run action, then choose Export Entries Action.
  2. Enter the staging upload ID in Destination project ID.
  3. Under Search options, choose All entries visible to me (visible), set Maximum entries to 10, and enter {} in Search query. Leave Archive required paths empty to export complete archives.
  4. Under Export options, choose json and keep Create ZIP archive enabled. Run the action.
  5. Open the created action instance to follow its status and logs. Once it succeeds, find exported_dir_path in Results.
  6. Open the destination project's files and download the ZIP at that relative path. Extract it to inspect data.json, selected_entries.json, and metadata.json.

Screencast placeholder

A screencast will demonstrate choosing Export Entries, completing these fields, monitoring the action, and downloading the ZIP. The written steps above are complete without it.

docs.title: Submit the same export with Python and REST
docs.text:
You need Python with requests installed, network access to the deployment's API, and a bearer token authorized to start actions and access the chosen entries and destination. The client does not need a local NOMAD installation or worker.

Save this as export_entries_input.json, replacing YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID:

{
  "upload_id": "YOUR_STAGING_UPLOAD_ID",
  "search_settings": {
    "owner": "visible",
    "max_entries": 10,
    "query": "{}",
    "required": []
  },
  "export_settings": {
    "file_format": "json",
    "create_zip_archive": true
  }
}

query is a string containing a JSON object. Here "{}" matches entries within the chosen ownership scope. Omit user_id; REST injects the authenticated user's ID before validating the action inputs and overwrites any supplied value.

Set NOMAD_API_URL to the deployment's API base URL, including /api/v1 (for example, https://YOUR_NOMAD_HOST/api/v1), and NOMAD_TOKEN to your bearer token in your shell environment. Save the following as submit_export.py and run python submit_export.py from the directory containing the input file:

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

import requests

api_url = os.environ['NOMAD_API_URL'].rstrip('/')
token = os.environ['NOMAD_TOKEN']
input_json = json.loads(Path('export_entries_input.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
action_id = 'nomad_ml_workflows.actions:export_entries'

response = requests.post(
    f'{api_url}/actions/{action_id}/start',
    headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'},
    json={'data': input_json},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json()['action_instance_id'])

The script submits the action and prints its instance ID. It does not wait for completion. Use that ID on the GUI action instance page, or make authenticated requests to GET /actions/{action_instance_id}/status and, after completion, GET /actions/{action_instance_id}/result, relative to the same API base URL. The result's exported_dir_path identifies the ZIP in your destination upload's raw files.

docs.title: Check the dataset
docs.text:
data.json contains a JSON array of records with entry IDs, upload IDs, and archives. selected_entries.json records the selected sources. In metadata.json, inspect data.num_entries_available, data.num_entries_selected, and data.num_entries_exported. With enough readable entries, the selected count is ten; fewer matches or skipped archives can produce fewer exported records.

If no entries match, the ZIP still contains an empty manifest and metadata, but no data.json. For selected archive paths, other formats, and directory output, continue with Export entries.
